title: Read N Characters Given Read4
statement:
The contents of a text file are hidden from you; the only access is a helper `read4(buf4)`. Every call to it copies up to 4 further characters of the file into the array `buf4`, beginning at index 0, moves its own private position in the file past them, and returns how many characters it copied: 4 while enough text remains, fewer at the end, and 0 once nothing is left.

With nothing but `read4`, write a reader `(buf, n)` that puts the first `n` characters of the file into `buf`, beginning at index 0, and returns how many it put there. That count is `n`, or the length of the file when the file is shorter than `n`. The reader is called only once per case, and `buf` has space for `n` characters.

Write `read(read4)`: it receives the `read4` helper and returns the reader function `(buf, n) => count`. Each case is written as `[file, n]`; your code never touches `file` directly. The result is the count your reader returns, and it only counts as correct when `buf[0..count-1]` holds exactly the file's first `count` characters.
constraints: file contains only English letters and digits
notes:
## Intuition

`read4` hands the file over in blocks of four, but the caller wants exactly `n` characters. So keep requesting blocks and move their characters into `buf` one at a time, stopping as soon as `n` have been delivered or a short block shows the file has run out. Pulling the whole file in first would also work, but it makes needless calls and keeps text nobody asked for.

## Approach

1. Create a 4-slot scratch array `buf4` and set `copied = 0`.
2. While fewer than `n` characters have been copied, call `read4(buf4)`; `count` is how many characters the block holds.
3. Copy characters from `buf4` to `buf[copied]`, stopping at the end of the block or as soon as `copied` reaches `n`.
4. A block with fewer than 4 characters means the file is exhausted, so leave the loop.
5. Return `copied`.

## Example 1, step by step

`file = "abc"`, `n = 4`. The first `read4` call fills `buf4` with `a`, `b`, `c` and returns `count = 3`. The inner loop copies all three into `buf[0..2]`, so `copied = 3`. Because `3 < 4`, the file is finished, the loop ends, and the reader returns `3` with `buf` starting `a b c`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): at most about n / 4 + 1 calls to `read4`, and each character is copied once.
- Space: O(1): only the 4-slot `buf4`.

## Pitfalls

- Stop in the middle of a block when `copied` reaches `n`: for `"abcd"` with `n = 3` the answer is 3, not 4.
- When the file length is a multiple of 4, the last full block is followed by a call that returns 0; `count < 4` must end the loop.
- Return the number actually copied, which is less than `n` for a short file.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `buf4` | scratch array that receives each block from `read4` |
| `count` | how many characters the latest block holds |
| `copied` | how many characters have been placed in `buf` |
| `i` | position inside the current block |

narration.2: read hands back the reader; the reader keeps access to read4 through the closure.
narration.3: A scratch array that receives each block from read4.
narration.4: Nothing has been placed in buf yet.
narration.6: Keep going until n characters have been copied.
narration.7: Fetch the next block of up to 4 characters.
narration.8: Walk through the block, but never past the n-th character overall.
narration.9: Put this character into the next free slot of buf.
narration.12: A short block means the file has ended, so stop asking for more.
narration.14: Report how many characters ended up in buf.
